title: How the Omni-Cause Swallowed Amnesty International
author: Julie Bindel
content:
![How the Omni-Cause Swallowed Amnesty
International](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/10/Screenshot-2026-10-09-at-7.26.01
---AM.png)

In July, Amnesty International UK
[_published_](https://archive.org/details/report-a-growing-threat-the-anti-
rights-movement-in-the-uk-july) a report called "A Growing Threat: The Anti-
Rights Movement in the UK." Written by Chiara Capraro, Amnesty's gender
justice director, the document prompted complaints from the organizations it
had labelled "anti-rights," among them feminist, lesbian, and gay groups
(including the [_Lesbian
Project_](https://www.thelesbianproject.co.uk/?ref=compactmag.com), which I
co-founded with Kathleen Stock) as well as a number of other bona fide human
rights organizations. The report's principal charge was "transphobia."

This was not the first time Amnesty had defamed organizations standing up for
the rights of women and girls. It had already
[_published_](https://web.archive.org/web/20260521101700/https:/media.amnesty.org.uk/documents/Like_a_snowball_final_.pdf)
"Like a Snowball: The Growth and Impact of the Gender-Critical Movement in the
UK" in May, though that report had gone largely unnoticed. One organization
named as "anti-rights" in both reports was [_Beira 's
Place_](https://beirasplace.org.uk/about/?ref=compactmag.com), which was
founded (and is solely funded) by author and philanthropist JK Rowling.

> "Longstanding supporters of Amnesty were dismayed."

As the reports circulated, longstanding supporters of Amnesty were dismayed
and outraged to see the organization turn on individuals, groups and services
that were, in the main, set up to counter human rights abuses against women.
Initially, Amnesty claimed that the report's "use of language does not reflect
the position of Amnesty International UK," and a spokesman said--implausibly--
that it had been "uploaded without going through the established internal
review processes that are in place to ensure consistency, accuracy and
alignment with Amnesty International UK's positions," adding that it remains
"committed to defending human rights, including both the rights of women and
the rights of trans people." Before long, the heat was turned up
significantly, especially when Rowling offered to fund any women's
organization wishing to take legal action against Amnesty. But the icing on
the cake was a strongly worded letter from lawyers for Beira's Place in mid-
July, demanding that the report be withdrawn, that a public apology be issued,
and that an external review examine how it had come to be published. On July
28, after new information had come to light, the Beira's Place lawyers sent a
second letter, this time warning that the organization had been "maliciously
defamed."

It wasn't just those directly affected by the reports who had objections.
Iseult White is the granddaughter of [_Se an
MacBride_](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/1974/macbride/facts/?ref=compactmag.com),
the Irish republican activist, politician, and diplomat who co-founded Amnesty
alongside Peter Benenson. She tells me she is "appalled" at the direction the
once revered human rights organization has taken. "Releasing that report," she
says, "is essentially a form of propaganda: designating groups as not worthy
of speech because they're 'anti-rights,' and not worthy of freedom of
association." Amnesty's "original approach," she adds, "was based on
meticulously researching a case, establishing that this was a prisoner of
conscience, and building a campaign around that: letter-writing, cards, and so
on. It was based on valid, real research. There's no research behind that
report; it's just a set of opinions." There is little question whose opinions
those are. In November 2025, when Capraro, the second report's author,
appeared on the Guilty Feminist
[_podcast_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yJw9nw8WSvc&ref=compactmag.com),
she said of the so-called anti-rights organizations: "In the same way that we
are a global feminist and human rights movement, they are like the dark side.
And they're smart, they work globally, they collaborate."
